reconstructed_theorem_text: For every integer n >= 3, let mu be normalized Haar probability measure on the full real orthogonal group O(n), with its Borel sigma-algebra. Let S be any subset of {0,...,n-1} that contains an index i different from 0. Let h: R -> R be Borel measurable, and assume that O -> h(O_{00}) is absolutely integrable with respect to mu. Write O[S,S] for the principal submatrix with row and column indices in S. Then O -> det(O[S,S]) h(O_{00}) is absolutely integrable with respect to mu, and integral_{O(n)} det(O[S,S]) h(O_{00}) dmu(O) = 0.
objects: The dimension n; the full orthogonal group O(n); its normalized Haar probability measure mu; a finite subset S of matrix indices; a selected index i in S; a real Borel measurable function h; the principal submatrix O[S,S]; and its determinant multiplied by h(O_{00}).
domains: n is a natural number with n >= 3. Matrix indices are {0,...,n-1}. S is a finite subset of those indices and i is one of those indices. O ranges over all real n by n orthogonal matrices, including determinant +1 and -1, with the inherited matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra. h maps R to R. All integrals use normalized Haar probability measure mu on the entire group O(n).
quantifiers: For every natural n >= 3, every finite S subset of {0,...,n-1}, every i in {0,...,n-1} satisfying i in S and i != 0, and every Borel measurable h: R -> R for which integral |h(O_{00})| dmu(O) is finite, both conclusions hold.
assumptions: n >= 3; i belongs to S; i != 0; h is Borel measurable; and the composition O -> h(O_{00}) is absolutely Bochner L1 integrable under normalized Haar probability measure on O(n). No boundedness or global real-line integrability of h is assumed.
conclusion: The function O -> det(O[S,S]) h(O_{00}) is absolutely Bochner L1 integrable under mu, and its integral over O(n) is zero.
scopes: The same n, S, i and h are fixed throughout both conclusions. Both appearances of O in each integrand refer to the same orthogonal matrix, and O is bound by the group integral or integrability assertion. O_{00} uses the zero-based first row and first column. The condition is existence of a chosen nonzero index in S; S need not contain 0. The measure is fixed as normalized Haar measure on the full compact group.
constant_dependencies: There are no existential or unspecified constants. The lower dimension bound is the fixed number 3, the distinguished coordinate is the fixed index 0, the integral is the fixed value 0, and the Haar law depends only on n.
